met_analysis:
The Western Disturbance as a cyclonic circulation over Himachal Pradesh & adjoining north Haryana now lies over northwest Uttar Pradesh between 1.5 to 5.8 km above mean sea level. However, trough aloft in upper tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 7.6 km above mean sea level roughly along Long. 77°E to the north of Lat. 27°N has moved away northeastwards.
A trough in upper tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 7.6 km above mean sea level runs roughly along Long. 80°E to the north of Lat. 24°N tilting northwestwards with height.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over south Bangladesh adjoining Gangetic West Bengal at 1.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The trough from northwest Bay of Bengal to East Uttar Pradesh across north Odisha, Jharkhand and southwest Bihar at 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over central Pakistan & neighbourhood now lies over West Rajasthan & neighbourhood at 1.5 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over East Rajasthan & neighbourhood at 0.9 km above mean sea level merged with the above cyclonic circulation.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over East Uttar Pradesh & neighbourhood at 4.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Gulf of Mannar & adjoining south Tamil Nadu coast at 0.9 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over south Andaman Sea & neighbourhood persists and now extending upto 5.8 km above mean sea level. Under its influence, a low-pressure area is likely to form over the Southeast Bay of Bengal around 13th October.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over south Kerala & neighbourhood at 0.9 km above mean sea level has become less marked.
